Welcome to Motions in Motion aspiring lawyers!

1. Select your case to play by voting, this is a democratic nation after all right?
2. Once the judge is selected, the judge should go and stand next to the host screen.
3. Once you've been split into teams, everyone go group up with their team and GET READY!
4. Once the game begins, one person from the prosecution team will be randomly selected to go up and deliver the initial argument, this is the time for the rest of the people on each team to send in motions to bring in evidence from their evidence pile, objections, etc. Remember that motions take time to get there since it's by car, and only one person can send motions at a time!!!
   1. Evidence motions, normal delivery speed
      1. Motion to bring forward evidence: select an evidence from your team's evidence pile and send it to court.
      2. Motion to suppress: select an evidence currently in the court and ask the judge to strike it down based on a provided argument.
   2. Objections, faster delivery speed
      1. Objection on the basis of Illegal Communication: Allows your team to talk temporarily over the other team on their speaking turn if the background lawyers are verbally speaking to the main speaking lawyer upfront.
      2. Objection on the basis of Poor Logic: Allows your team to speak temporarily on why the other team who is speaking's basic logic or interpretation of evidence is unsound for any reason during the other team's speaking turn.
   3. Sending in notes, slower delivery speed
      1. Send in a note to the speaker to help them.
5. When you send in evidence, it is sent in by car. You first choose a body, which is the base speed of the car (the motion bonus is added on to get the total speed), but each car body can only be used once per game. Then, you must DRAW the wheels of the car, draw so it will be best suited to get over obstacles, and once that is done, send the car off with your motion.
6. Once the timer is done the case is complete and the judge must make a final verdict of guilty on all charges, guilty on one charge, or not guilty.
